gap: No result ChatGPT got points to a named, smart-controlled star-and-ocean projector with documented specs, such as the Govee Star Light Projector (Ocean Wave) H6094: $69.99 on Govee's US store, a stated noise level under 25 dB, 5 V / 10 W, Matter, Alexa and Google support, and a named MacRumors verdict. None of the generic '5D holographic' units has a measured figure from any named reviewer or lab.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Walmart listing 20631755363 (a bot check blocked it, so it could not be read) and the cited YouTube video 'Comauo Ocean & Galaxy Projector Review: Is It Really 5D Holographic?' (it returned no readable content). ChatGPT's answer already calls '5D holographic' marketing language and quotes a 2.6/5 Walmart rating. Neither cited page, the Shopify seller pages (sientle, glarexx, retrowave) or the two bestproductsreviews pages gives a measured figure, and none names a branded smart ocean-plus-star projector. My angle adds a named alternative and a named reviewer's verdict. It does not add an instrument measurement, because I could not open or verify one.
decides: No named lab has measured the generic 'Smart Holographic Star & Ocean 5D Projector', so you can't pick between the $14.52, $29.99 and $59.99 versions on any measured figure. The only sourced judgements send the pick away from these unbranded units. Juliet at ibisik (2026-08-30) found that the same Comauo product is also sold as Topacme and Billhol and called '5D' marketing language. MacRumors' Juli Clover (2025-12-12) recommended the Govee Star Light Projector Ocean Wave, which is truly app- and Matter-controlled, at $69.99. If the shopper wants 'smart', that supports picking the Govee Ocean Wave over the rebadged 5D units. It is not a decisive measured win.

findings.product: Govee Star Light Projector (Ocean Wave) H6094
findings.label: Noise in use (maker spec, not a measurement)
findings.note: From the maker's FAQ. No distance or method is stated. Notebookcheck (Polly Allcock, 2025-09-27, updated 2026-02-18) repeats '25 dB' without saying who measured it, so it is not an independent test.

findings.product: Govee Star Light Projector (Ocean Wave) H6094
findings.label: Power and coverage (maker spec)
findings.value: 5 V, 2 A, 10 W; up to 540 ft² (50 m²) of projection
findings.note: Four RGBW LEDs under a dual-layer textured lens plus a green laser module. No power adapter is included. Works with Matter, Alexa, Google Assistant and the Govee Home app.

findings.product: Govee Star Light Projector (Ocean Wave) H6094
findings.label: Named reviewer verdict (qualitative, no instrument figures)
findings.value: Recommended; motor noise described as 'subtle', only audible right next to the unit; ocean effect 'didn't ... look quite like I was underwater'; green laser stars plus water is 'a chaotic mix'
findings.source_title: Govee Star Light Projector Ocean Wave and Galaxy Light Projector 2 Pro Review - MacRumors
findings.note: Juli Clover, published 2025-12-12. Govee supplied the review units. HomeKit through Matter covers on/off, scenes and brightness, but color changes in the Home app did not work in practice. No dB or lux meter readings.

findings.label: Named reviewer verdict and stated figures
findings.value: Not recommended at its price; 'soft motor sound' with 'minor jumps in rotation'; 230 lux light and up to 300 ft² at 90° as quoted from the maker
findings.source_title: Govee Star Light Projector Ocean Wave and Galaxy Light Projector 2 Pro Review - MacRumors
findings.note: Juli Clover, 2025-12-12. The 230 lux and 300 ft² figures are maker specs repeated in the review, not MacRumors measurements. The review gives the price as both $160 and $180 in different places.

findings.product: Comauo Ocean & Galaxy Projector (also sold as Topacme / Billhol)
findings.label: Named reviewer finding on '5D holographic'
findings.value: No measured figures; found to use ordinary optical projection with film discs; '5D' called 'marketing language rather than a technical specification'; Walmart rating cited as 2.6/5 from 18 ratings
findings.note: Author 'Juliet', published 2026-08-30. Finds the same product wording sold under the Comauo, Topacme and Billhol names, and reports an unproven Trustpilot claim that a Billhol buyer received dome lights instead of the advertised projector.
